chapter: Taped excerpts: friends, family and facts
title: Writing 'Louisiana' with Andy Razaf
summary: Neither man had been to Louisiana when they wrote the song, and Johnson calls Razaf prolific and brilliant.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh-huh. J. C., remember we were talking a while back about the song, 'Louisiana,' and I told you we got a letter ask -- telling us that they would -- they want to get in touch with you because they like to make that their state anthem?
And I asked you if you had been to Louisiana, and you said yes, but you weren't there when you wrote 'Louisiana.'
And do you remember the circumstances, how you happened to write 'Louisiana'?
Just wrote it (inaudible) and I wrote it, And I (inaudible). Nothing unusual about writing a song in those days. You wrote them or you didn't write them.
Yeah. Yeah. I know that Mary Butler told me that's her favorite song of all your songs. She just --
She just loved it. Now, how about Andy? Had he been to Louisiana?
In other words, he just wrote it out of his, you know, imagination?
Oh, Andy was -- he was a prolific writer, terrific. He was very -- he was a pretty brilliant person on top of it.
You could just do about most anything with a lyric.
